Why? I love being able to choose a language depending on the project I'm working on. Imagine being forced to use Java or Ada everywhere. I don't know about you, but I'd rush to become an hair stylist... There's a reason why new languages keep popping up: there may be a better way to solve a problem. Expecting to be able to solve every problems with one tool is, IMO, foolish.

Also, you'll take my life before you take emacs away from me.

Though it is not a popular thing to say, Adobe was on the path to this with Flex/FlashBuilder/AIR until the Flash hate and Steve Jobs' lies made them doubt the plan. Flex and its companion runtime AIR were able to build applications for Windows, MacOX, Android and iOS targets with one code base. For a while there was Linux support for AIR apps too but the demand was not there. The Adobe roadmap for Flex/Flash included a Flash VM that would have enabled server-side development as well. To this day I think the idea was a good one and the language, framework and to a lesser extent the IDE were all working together very well. I miss building RIAs (rich internet applications) in Flex because I could make awesome stuff in far less time than HTML, CSS and JS-frameworks-du-jour and with more pizzazz and functionality. One day I hope we revisit this idea but I don't think Open Source can get there. There is no incentive in Open Source to build a single, strong and well built platform like this and everyone will just fork new variants that don't really add anything to the project. Closed source software was able to mature these things and make solid foundations but everyone hates closed source now. Sigh.
